text: The seven sixty-seven is now a very heavy glider. But its controls are moved by hydraulic pressure, and the pumps were powered by the engines. So, from the belly of the plane, a small propeller drops out into the wind. The ram air turbine. The rushing air spins it, and it drives a hydraulic pump, just enough to move the controls. Just enough. No flaps, no slats, and the plane gets harder to steer as it slows down.
